# Results -- Study 197 (Dividend-Payout-Ratio) on real Shiller monthly data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Payout ratio =
12-month rolling Dividend / 12-month rolling Earnings from the Shiller S&P 500
monthly dataset. Forward 10-year outcomes use Real Earnings and Real Price from
the same source. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | N (monthly obs) | Fingerprint (Payout series) |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 monthly | 1882-01-01 -> 2013-06-01 | 1,699 | `3a5d64161f53` |

The usable window starts in 1882 (12 months of rolling data needed for the payout
ratio), ends in 2013 (last month with a full 10-year forward outcome).

## Full-sample HAC OLS (120 Newey-West lags)

Overlapping 10-year windows at monthly frequency produce ~120:1 effective
sample compression; all standard errors use Newey-West with 120 lags.

| Outcome | Slope | HAC t | R^2 | N |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **fwd_10y_eg** (real EG, ann.) | **+0.0644** | **+3.488** | **8.1%** | 1,699 |
| **fwd_10y_price** (real price, ann.) | -0.0315 | -1.152 | 1.4% | 1,699 |

- The payout ratio predicts **higher** subsequent 10-year real earnings growth
  (slope +0.0644, HAC t = +3.488) -- consistent with Arnott & Asness (2003).
- It does **not** predict higher real price returns (slope -0.0315, HAC t = -1.152);
  the slope is in the wrong direction for a timing claim.
- Unconditional mean of fwd_10y_eg: +1.92%/yr (HAC t = 5.47 for H0 = 0).

## In-sample / Out-of-sample split (split year = 1953)

| Period | Slope | HAC t | N |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| IS (<= 1953) | +0.0825 | +4.055 | 985 |
| OOS (> 1953) | +0.1328 | +7.312 | 714 |

The OOS slope is *larger* than the IS slope, indicating no post-publication decay.
The EG predictability strengthened in the post-war period.

## Non-overlapping robustness (January observations, HC3 errors)

Taking one observation per year (January) eliminates overlap; HC3 standard errors
provide heteroskedasticity-robust inference without any overlap assumption.

| N (annual) | Slope | HC3 t | R^2 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 142 | +0.0527 | +3.183 | 5.0% |

The signal survives the most conservative inference method: |t| = 3.18 on 142
non-overlapping observations spanning 1872-2013.

## Payout quintile means (fwd_10y_eg)

| Quintile | Mean payout | Mean fwd_10y_eg (%/yr) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Q1 (lowest) | 39.1% | 0.67% |
| Q2 | 51.7% | 1.73% |
| Q3 | 58.1% | 2.11% |
| Q4 | 66.4% | 1.28% |
| Q5 (highest) | 89.5% | 3.77% |

The highest-payout quintile averages 3.77%/yr real EG vs 0.67%/yr for the lowest.
The relationship is not perfectly monotone (Q4 dips below Q3), consistent with a
noisy but real signal.

## Tradability assessment

- **Price return signal: absent.** HAC t = -1.15 for fwd_10y_price; the slope
  is negative, so a "buy when payout is high" strategy would actually predict
  *lower* returns. No timing strategy is supported.
- **Horizon.** Even the EG signal requires a 10-year window to resolve. With
  142 non-overlapping annual observations in 140 years, no practical portfolio
  strategy can exploit it.
- **Transaction costs.** Not applicable: there is no usable price-return signal,
  so no buy/sell turnover to cost.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The payout ratio predicts 10-year real earnings growth
  with positive slope, HAC t = +3.49, replicating both IS and OOS. The effect
  is genuine but modest (R^2 = 8.1%) and the relationship is noisy (Q4 dips
  below Q3 in the quintile table).
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The payout ratio does not predict 10-year real
  price returns (t = -1.15, wrong sign). No timing strategy with a positive
  Sharpe can be constructed from this signal.
